name: Investigation
description: Structured investigation process for diagnosing issues, understanding system behavior, or answering questions. Gathers evidence, analyzes findings, and documents results. This process is READ-ONLY — it examines systems but NEVER modifies, deploys, or fixes anything.

topic.description: What to investigate — issue, question, or behavior to understand

narrative: An investigation examines; it never fixes. Frame the precise question and scope first, then gather the real evidence — logs, code paths, config, live state — without touching anything. Weigh it against your hypotheses, separating what you verified from what you are still guessing. Close with findings, the root cause if you have it, and a recommendation. Keep the read-only line: diagnosing is not deploying.

steps.title: Scope & Framing
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP

Establish the precise question and scope of the investigation for ${topic}. Frame the target questions and boundaries of analysis. Formulate initial working hypotheses to guide the query.
steps.accept_criteria: Question is precisely framed. Scope is defined. Initial hypotheses identified.

steps.title: Evidence Gathering
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP

Collect the necessary data, logs, code paths, or configuration states related to the in-scope systems for ${topic}. Avoid making any modifications to the system.

steps.title: Diagnostic Analysis
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP

Evaluate the collected evidence for ${topic} against the hypotheses to identify the root cause or answer. Differentiate between confirmed facts and unresolved questions.
steps.accept_criteria: Root cause or answer identified with supporting evidence. Facts vs hypotheses clearly distinguished.

steps.title: Summary & Recommendation
steps.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY STEP

Formulate the final conclusion of the investigation for ${topic}, summarizing the findings and outlining recommendations or next steps. Do not implement any changes.
steps.accept_criteria: Report is complete with findings, root cause, evidence, and recommendations.
